primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: KCNJ2 encodes Kir2.1, an inward-rectifier potassium channel important for setting and stabilizing skeletal/cardiac resting membrane potential and for terminal cardiac repolarization. Pathogenic variants can exert dominant-negative effects that reduce Kir2.1 current.
vignette: A 16-year-old girl has recurrent episodes of flaccid weakness and frequent premature ventricular complexes. Holter monitoring shows runs of bidirectional ventricular tachycardia. Examination shows low-set ears, micrognathia, and clinodactyly. Genetic testing identifies a pathogenic variant in KCNJ2.
lead: The protein affected in this patient normally has which of the following functions?
correct: It conducts an inward-rectifier potassium current that stabilizes resting membrane potential and contributes to terminal cardiac repolarization
distractors: It conducts the rapid delayed-rectifier potassium current responsible for much of phase 3 repolarization
It forms the cardiac sodium channel that produces the rapid phase 0 upstroke
It serves as the ryanodine-sensitive sarcoplasmic-reticulum calcium-release channel
It carries the hyperpolarization-activated pacemaker current in sinoatrial nodal cells
distractor_notes: The rapid delayed-rectifier potassium current is mediated primarily by channels containing hERG/KCNH2, not Kir2.1/KCNJ2.
The major fast cardiac sodium channel is Nav1.5 encoded by SCN5A, not KCNJ2.
RYR2 forms the cardiac ryanodine receptor responsible for sarcoplasmic-reticulum calcium release; it is not the KCNJ2 gene product.
HCN channels mediate the funny/pacemaker current in nodal tissue; KCNJ2 encodes the inward-rectifier Kir2.1 channel.
key_expl: Andersen-Tawil syndrome is strongly associated with KCNJ2 variants. KCNJ2 encodes Kir2.1, an inward-rectifier K+ channel expressed in cardiac and skeletal muscle. Kir2.1 helps establish/stabilize the resting membrane potential and contributes importantly to the terminal repolarization phase of the cardiac action potential.
objective: Identify Kir2.1/KCNJ2 as an inward-rectifier potassium channel that stabilizes muscle resting membrane potential and terminal cardiac repolarization.
